reviews.title: Upgrades? More like downgrades.
reviews.text: With the new update, at least on the mobile version, now when you click onto a plane, the flight number and aircraft type no longer show. Alongside this new change, the font size of the information regarding the flights speed & altitude etc has also become smaller to the point where it just looks unnatural and accidental, almost as if it isn’t meant to be so small. Not to mention the adverts that appear every 15-20 clicks. Perhaps flightradar should never update their app as the app’s quality seems to diminish with every one.

reviews.title: Ruined by corporate greed
reviews.text:
This app used to be amazing, but now it has been overran by corporate greed with aggressive data mining and selling, even when you opt out of it. I have always been opted out of your tracking, but I am still getting numerous data deletion request alerts with data packages traced back to this app. Shame on you guys. A user of over a decade but I value my privacy over your bottom line so I will never be using your service again. Shame on you all.

Responding to your reply: you are full of it and you know it. As a gold subscriber of several years I have cancelled my subscription and am moving onto other platforms. The fact that you sell so much data to third parties has not only made me delete this app and cancel my subscription, the company I work for, which is actually an aviation repair and service provider, actually has your website blocked on their servers and categorized as spyware. My company has us use other, safer alternatives. Again this platform has been destroyed by corporate greed.

reviews.title: DO NOT UPDATE THIS APP!!
reviews.text: Just want to say a big THANK YOU to all the review writers who posted their bad experiences after updating this app. I’m sorry you all suffered, but I thank you for informing the rest of us so we don’t make the same mistake. To the developers: Taking away features from existing users is reprehensible. You really should be ashamed of yourselves. I don’t have a problem supporting developers when they make a good product, but it is incredibly unprofessional to retroactively go back and try to charge people for services that you gave away for free when they signed up for them. If you didn’t want to give it away for free, you never should have done so in the first place. Nobody cares about your canned story about rising costs. There’s an honorable way to do business and a dishonorable way. You chose the wrong one. Edit: Expected a canned response, wasn’t disappointed. You can’t spin your way out of disreputable business practices. I really wish people would wake up to this nonsense and stop rewarding shady businesses for this reprehensible behavior.

reviews.title: Spammy, grubby ads
reviews.text: I have used this app over many years purely out of interest to identify planes overhead, therefore I don’t need the paid version. But recently it has turned to the dark side and I was presented with a rather spammy-looking mock up of a Google page informing me “We have detected your iPhone has been infected with viruses. It (sic) will soon corrupt your SIM card, data, photos and contacts if no immediate action is taken”, inviting me to click a button to clean my virus-ridden phone. No thanks. In typical fashion, another formerly respected app has sadly turned to these grubby monetisation tactics. Deleted immediately.

reviews.title: To many Ads
reviews.text:
This used to be a great app with a nice balance of ads for free users. The ads were quick and didn’t get in the way of actually using the app. Lately, though, the experience has gotten much worse.

Now ads pop up almost immediately when opening the app, which is especially frustrating when you’re trying to quickly check a plane flying overhead. The ads also take longer to get through, often requiring multiple taps just to close them. By the time you finally get back to the app, the plane you were trying to identify has already passed.

The increase in ads and how intrusive they’ve become is really hurting the usability. What was once a smooth and useful app is starting to feel frustrating and unreliable for its main purpose. Lately I’ve even considered just deleting this app and looks for something else because it’s gotten to frustrating to use.

reviews.title: A once good app now totally unbearable
reviews.text: I’ve used flight radar for many years. Several years ago, it had a major upgrade and as a paid app user, I was booted down to the free version. Out of principle I wasn’t going to fork out again for something I’d already paid for. The free version of the app with its more limited info has been usable until recently but now the intrusive ads have ruined it. The ads are so long and after being exposed to what feels like over a minute of ads, there’s no way to kill off the ad (no x appears). In fact it insists on taking you to the page to buy the stupid game it’s promoting! then you get stuck in a perpetual loop of ad and purchase page. The only way to exit the intolerable ads is to kill off the app and reload it - losing the plane you were tracking. It’s sad because this was once so good but now the greediness has made it unusable.
